strategies.name: Trend + Carry
strategies.blurb: The book that trades today. Cross-asset trend and carry, with the meta-label filter, the regime de-risk and the t-statistic trend signal.
strategies.about: About 23 liquid ETFs across stocks, bonds, credit, commodities and currencies. One sleeve follows trends over 3, 6 and 12 months; the other holds a risk-parity income book tilted by the yield curve. A small classifier skips the weakest trend entries, exposure is halved when the S&P is below its 200-day average in a volatile market, and the whole book is scaled to 8% annual volatility.
strategies.outcome: Every piece was added only after it passed the alpha gate on its own. The last change, a trend signal sized by its t-statistic instead of its sign, cut trend turnover by a fifth. It has paper-traded from June 2026; the record for this exact version starts 2026-10-08.

strategies.name: Trend + Carry, with regime de-risk
strategies.blurb: The previous live version, before the t-statistic trend signal. Same book, with the original sign-based trend rule.
strategies.about: The full stack as deployed in June: base book, meta-label filter and the regime de-risk, scaled to 8% volatility. The trend rule takes the average sign of 3-, 6- and 12-month returns, so every trend gets a full-size position however weak it is.
strategies.outcome: Ran live from June to October 2026. Replaced in v44 by the same book with a t-statistic trend signal, which earned more per unit of risk and traded less.

strategies.name: Trend + Carry, with meta-labeling
strategies.blurb: The base book plus a small classifier that decides which trend signals to act on.
strategies.about: Meta-labeling leaves the trend rule alone and trains a shallow XGBoost model, walk-forward, to veto entries that look weak. It never predicts prices. Out of sample it was right only a little more often than a coin (AUC about 0.52), which turned out to be enough.
strategies.outcome: It raised the Sharpe ratio, and bigger models did worse than the small one. At 8% volatility it also deepened the worst drawdown, which is what the regime de-risk was built to fix.

strategies.name: Trend + Carry base book
strategies.blurb: The two sleeves blended by risk, before any overlay. The first version that was paper-traded.
strategies.about: Trend and carry, weighted by inverse volatility with a tilt toward the sleeve with the better recent Sharpe ratio, rebalanced monthly. Nothing is fitted to the data, so the whole history counts as out of sample.
strategies.outcome: Passed every robustness check we had: resampled histories, twelve parameter changes and seven crisis windows. Adding 28 more ETFs made it worse, so the universe stayed small.

strategies.name: Cross-asset trend
strategies.blurb: Long what has been rising, short what has been falling, across asset classes. The first idea that worked.
strategies.about: For each ETF, average the sign of its 3-, 6- and 12-month returns and size the position so each asset carries the same risk. Trend following has a century of evidence behind it and tends to make money in long sell-offs.
strategies.outcome: Barely correlated with the S&P 500, and it beat the index in four of five crisis windows (2008: +7.1% against −43.4%). That made it the foundation of the book.

strategies.name: Carry and defensive sleeve
strategies.blurb: A long-only, risk-balanced income book, leaning toward bonds when the yield curve pays for it.
strategies.about: Holds bonds, credit, gold and equities in risk-parity weights, tilted by the gap between 10-year and 3-month Treasury yields. It earns a steady premium in calm markets, which is where trend struggles.
strategies.outcome: Its returns moved almost independently of trend (correlation +0.13), so blending the two gave a smoother book than either on its own.

strategies.name: S&P stock momentum
strategies.blurb: Buy the S&P 500 stocks that rose most over the past year. Too small an edge to survive costs.
strategies.about: The classic cross-sectional momentum trade on point-in-time S&P 500 members, rebalanced monthly and volatility-targeted, filled at the next open with 7 bps of cost.
strategies.outcome: An earlier run looked good until we found five corrupted price days in 2010–11 that carried the whole result. On clean data it barely beat cash and lost to buy-and-hold.

strategies.name: Post-earnings drift
strategies.blurb: Trade S&P stocks in the direction of a big earnings surprise and ride the drift. The return turned out to be market exposure.
strategies.about: After a large earnings surprise, prices are said to keep drifting the same way for weeks. The sleeve goes long when a stock gaps up more than two ATRs on earnings and short when it gaps down, holding for 45 trading days unless a stop is hit.
strategies.outcome: Regressed on the S&P 500, its return was all market beta (0.36) and its alpha was negative, about −3% a year. Holding the index would have done better.

strategies.name: S&P short-term reversal
strategies.blurb: Buy the S&P 500's recent losers and short its winners, betting on a bounce. Costs ate it.
strategies.about: The engine this project started with: rank S&P 500 stocks on their last few days of returns, buy the losers and short the winners, beta-neutral, rebalanced often.
strategies.outcome: Lost money with a drawdown over 50%. The S&P 500 is the most heavily traded universe there is, and a daily edge there is smaller than the cost of trading it.

strategies.name: Graph-clustering stat-arb, as published
strategies.blurb: A 2024 paper's 49%-a-year strategy, run with the paper's own settings. It hardly ever traded.
strategies.about: Clusters S&P 500 stocks with a signed-graph method, then trades short-term reversals inside each cluster, long the laggards and short the leaders, when a classifier trusts both sides. Run here with the paper's settings, including fills at the same close that produced the signal.
strategies.outcome: Against a claimed 49% a year it lost a little. The classifier almost never trusted the short side, so it traded on 4 of 228 rebalances, and the paper's two best tickers were symbols later reused by different companies.

strategies.name: Graph-clustering stat-arb, realistic
strategies.blurb: The same strategy with clean prices and next-morning fills, hedged with SPY so it trades at all.
strategies.about: With clean prices, next-open fills at 7 bps and a classifier retrained walk-forward, the strategy never traded, because it needs a long and a short leg. This pre-registered variant shorts SPY in place of the missing short leg to show what the long side was worth.
strategies.outcome: It lost about 12.5% a year. Whatever the paper found, it does not survive realistic trading.

strategies.name: S&P 500 (SPY)
strategies.blurb: Buy and hold the S&P 500, for reference.

strategies.name: 60/40 stocks and bonds
strategies.blurb: 60% SPY and 40% intermediate Treasuries (IEF), rebalanced daily, for reference.
